11. The Great Inventor

ledger.why: the casting line (the roles carry it)

collection.description: A villager has written a proud poem about the sea in which nearly every line ends with the word moon.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has written a poem. It is about the sea, the moon, and the mysterious beauty of coconuts. Unfortunately, nearly every line ends with the word "moon." (subject) is extremely proud of it and asks (friend) for an opinion.

a.name: Answer A
a.text: "It's very enthusiastic," says (friend). "Perhaps you could use a different word occasionally?" (subject) considers this and replaces one occurrence of "moon" with "spoon." The poem now makes considerably less sense. (subject) likes it even more.

b.name: Answer B
b.text: (friend) says that the poem is certainly unlike anything (friend.he/she) has heard before. (subject) beams. That evening (subject.he/she) begins a second poem, this time about fish. (friend) hopes it will contain fewer moons.
